test_title: PYST 40 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The jury, after a long deliberation, has finally reached a verdict in the high-profile case.

options.text: A verdict in the high-profile case has finally been reached by the jury after a long deliberation.
A verdict in the high-profile case was finally reached by the jury after a long deliberation.
A verdict in the high-profile case had been finally reached by the jury after a long deliberation.
A verdict in the high-profile case is discovered by the jury after a long deliberation.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The jury, after a long deliberation, has finally reached a verdict in the high-profile case."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a verdict in the high-profile case" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "has reached" to "has been reached" (present perfect passive).
 
• Preserve the time sequence and additional phrases, such as "after a long deliberation" and "by the jury," for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"A verdict in the high-profile case has finally been reached by the jury after a long deliberation."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"A verdict in the high-profile case was finally reached by the jury after a long deliberation." – Incorrect past tense usage (past simple instead of present perfect).
 
• **Option 3: **"A verdict in the high-profile case had been finally reached by the jury after a long deliberation." – Incorrect tense (past perfect instead of present perfect).
 
• **Option 4: **"A verdict in the high-profile case is discovered by the jury after a long deliberation." – Incorrect verb choice (present simple instead of present perfect).
